rendered: The premise is reversed on capacity. The document reports the discharge capacities as 212 mAh g^− 1 (10% Mn) vs 164 mAh g^− 1[1], so the least Mn-rich sample had the higher capacity and the most Mn-rich sample the lower. On heat, the most Mn-rich sample released less, not more. The thermal decomposition values are 901.4 J g^−1 for 10% Mn vs[2] and 485.7 J g^−1 for 50% Mn[3]. The difference between these values is 415.7[4] J per gram, so the most Mn-rich sample released that much less heat than the least Mn-rich sample. The text also says that lower Mn content generated less heat, which conflicts with its own numbers. The heat-flow peaks in Fig. 4[5] give the same per-gram values for each composition.
